items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, health sciences, psychology, public health, counseling, or a related field and or equivalent experience/training
Experience developing, implementing and assessing health promotion efforts related to collegiate recovery and alcohol and other drug risk reduction initiatives, preferably in a university setting.
Knowledge of higher education administration, public administration, student development or related ﬁeld, typically acquired through education and/or equivalent experience.

Experience with current and traditional theories of college and community health promotion, environmental change, behavior change and evaluation, and skill to apply them to a college student population.
Experience and training in Public Health and Health Promotion.
Experience with community organizing strategies and principles for prompting collective action.

Under general direction of the Associate Director of Health Equity and Wellbeing, the Risk and Prevention Specialist has overall responsibility for project oversight, coordination, and implementation of all alcohol and other drug risk reduction initiatives, including the collegiate recovery program. This position designs and conducts campus-wide risk reduction and health promotion initiatives using environmental management policy and institutional practice change strategies to improve student health status and support student success.
40% - Develop and Implement Programs and Interventions at The Individual Community, Organizational and Policy Level

The Risk and Prevention Specialist will focus on best practice models, including harm reduction strategies, sober curiosity approaches, and moderation techniques in recovery. This role requires a comprehensive understanding of health disparities affecting marginalized and underserved populations. The specialist will also emphasize the importance of reducing stigma and fostering inclusion through trauma-informed practices.
20% - Evaluate Effectiveness of Health Promotion Initiatives
Demonstrated skills to train and supervise student employees and volunteers.
Advanced level program planning, implementation and evaluation skills.
Interpersonal skills and political acumen to clearly and effectively interact with individuals of varying ages, cultural backgrounds, genders, sexual orientations, and perspectives.
Knowledge of current evidence-informed strategies and theories to change health behaviors and reduce risks, particularly among college students.
